target.title: fix: default TLS gateway deep links to port 443 when port is omitted
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an `openclaw://gateway` deep link with TLS enabled and no explicit port parsed to port **18789** instead of the standard TLS port **443**.

Setup codes and raw gateway URL parsing in OpenClawKit already default omitted TLS/WSS ports to 443; the `openclaw://gateway` query parser did not.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the same TLS default-port rule as setup-code and URL parsing in `DeepLinks.swift` (`tls ? 443 : 18789`) for the gateway deep-link query path.

The change preserves explicit ports, so existing links such as `openclaw://gateway?...&port=18789&tls=1` still parse to 18789.

## User Impact

TLS gateway deep links from QR codes or shared links can stage the expected HTTPS/WSS endpoint without requiring an explicit `port=443` parameter. On iOS, parsed gateway links are staged for gateway setup. The macOS handler currently parses `.gateway` links but does not apply them, so this PR scopes the user-flow claim to the shared parser and iOS setup path.

## Evidence

Parity source in OpenClawKit:

- `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/DeepLinks.swift` (setup-code and raw URL paths already use `tls ? 443 : 18789`)

Added regression tests:

- `DeepLinksSecurityTests.gatewayDeepLinkUsesTlsDefaultPortWhenPortMissing`
- `DeepLinksSecurityTests.gatewayDeepLinkPreservesExplicitTlsPort`

Rebase/conflict refresh:

- Rebased onto latest `origin/main` after `debugDashboardDeepLinkParses` landed.
- Kept both the new debug dashboard test and the gateway TLS tests.

Proof gap:

- I do not currently have redacted real iOS device/simulator deep-link proof. The PR has parser-level regression coverage and will rely on CI for `macos-swift` / `ios-build` after the branch refresh.
